standards.mechanism: IAM policy documents as templatefile() JSON templates
Reading the templates with the System.Text.Json DOM (JsonDocument)
Names looked up in AWS's programmatic service reference (public JSON, no credentials)
Action wildcards (* any characters, ? one), case-insensitive names, condition keys and the OIDC federation keys
Connect timeout and no redirects on SocketsHttpHandler; per-request timeout with HttpClient.Timeout
Retrying only the idempotent GET, at most twice, on curl --retry's transient failures (connection failure, timeout, 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) with its 1 s then 2 s back-off
Whole-check deadline as one CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter linked to the test's token
User-Agent product token (the reference answers 403 without one)
Testing HttpClient code with a stub HttpMessageHandler
The fetched reference shared as an xUnit class fixture (IClassFixture, IAsyncLifetime)
Recorded one-time OIDC subject check through the repository OIDC customization API

test_results.command: from infra/tests: scripts/test-lock.sh run stack 8.16 -- dotnet test --project DisputeDesk.PlatformTests --report-xunit-trx --results-directory <worktree>/TestResults

assumptions: The client sends one header, User-Agent: DisputeDesk-PlatformTests. Inputs say 'no ... extra header', but servicereference.us-east-1.amazonaws.com answers 403 to a request without a User-Agent (checked with curl -H 'User-Agent:'), and 7.16's curl sent its own. No credential, cookie or other header is sent; Fetch_ValidFiles_ReadsTheNamedServicesFromTheDocumentedLayout asserts the request headers are exactly User-Agent.

Retries cover curl --retry's transient set (connection failure, per-request timeout, 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504). Any other non-success, a redirect included, fails at once, so the index pointed at v1/no-such-file.json fails after one request.
The OIDC exception compares the two keys case-insensitively: criterion 4 says each key is looked up case-insensitively, as 7.16 did.

The real bounds are asserted as values: 30 s request timeout, 10 s connect timeout, no redirect, no cookies, no credentials and 2 retries in CreateClient_HasTheBoundsInTheStory. The 5-minute deadline is a constant in ServiceReferenceFixture. Behaviour on each side of each bound is tested with short timeouts and deadlines against a stub handler, so no test waits 30 s or 5 minutes, and no FakeTimeProvider package is added (the story adds no packages).
The retry back-off is a parameter of ServiceReference.FetchAsync: 1 s in the fixture, zero in the offline tests.

envs/dev/tests/deploy_role.tftest.hcl's header comment still says the policies are 'written with jsonencode'. It is now stale but left as it is, because the story requires every *.tftest.hcl unchanged. This is a candidate for the epic's lows.
Comments that sat inside the jsonencode() instance policy (EncryptKeyRing, XRayOtlpSpans) moved to the comment above aws_iam_role_policy.instance, because JSON has no comments.
The compute trust policy has no placeholders. It is rendered with templatefile(path, {}), so every policy attribute follows the one anchored rule.

Trivy reads neither the old jsonencode() inline role policies nor the templates for IAM wildcard checks. With an Allow */* statement added to a throwaway copy of modules/compute, both forms give the same single AWS-0104 finding, so Trivy loses no coverage.
The stale allowlist entry 'shell(infra/terraform/iam-names.test.sh)' in scripts/verify-with-copilot.sh:38 is left, because that file is outside the story's Touches.
No test asserts that ci.yml holds no id-token: write. AC7 is CI and docs, verified by grep and actionlint, and the story asks for no such check.
conflicts: Inputs ('no credential, cookie or extra header') versus the service reference, which refuses a request without a User-Agent (HTTP 403): resolved by sending only a User-Agent product token, as 7.16's curl did. See assumptions.
